inputs.statement: p is an arbitrary prime, K is an arbitrary field with Char K=p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

V is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module of highest weight λ and complex dimension λ+1. Its endomorphisms x,y,h satisfy hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y and xy−yx=h. The vector v∈V is nonzero and satisfies xv=0 and hv=λv.
Let K be a field, U a finite-dimensional K-vector space, ι a finite type, and v:ι→U a linearly independent family. If card ι=dim_K U, then span_K(range v)=U.

output.statement: For i=0,…,λ, the vectors e_i=y^iv/i! form a complex basis of V. They satisfy xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. For every r≥0, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and zero otherwise.

argument.text: By H001, λ is nonnegative, so natural bounds use λ.toNat=λ and n=λ+1. For every natural i, induction gives h y^i v=(λ−2i)y^i v: at i=0 this is hv=λv; if it holds at i, then hy^(i+1)v=(yh−2y)y^iv=(λ−2i−2)y^(i+1)v. Independently, x y^i v=i(λ−i+1)y^(i−1)v for i≥1. At i=1, xyv=yxv+hv=λv. Assuming this formula at i≥1, the preceding h formula gives xy^(i+1)v=(yx+h)y^iv=[i(λ−i+1)+λ−2i]y^iv=(i+1)(λ−i)y^iv. Both induction assumptions are discharged in their steps. Iterating the x formula for 0≤i≤λ gives x^iy^iv=i!·∏_(t=0)^(i−1)(λ−t)v. Every factor is a positive integer in C for i≥1 in this range; for i=0 the scalar is one. Since v≠0, y^iv and e_i are nonzero. Dividing the first formula by i! gives he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

produces.statement: For every natural q, hy^qv=(λ−2q)y^qv; for q≥1, xy^qv=q(λ−q+1)y^(q−1)v. For 0≤q≤λ, e_q≠0 and he_q=(λ−2q)e_q.

argument.text: To test independence, fix arbitrary a and temporarily assume L1: Σ_(i=0)^λ a_i e_i=0. For arbitrary j in the range apply ∏_(k=0,k≠j)^λ(h−(λ−2k)Id_V). The h-eigenvector formula F001 makes all summands except j vanish. The remaining equation is a_j ∏_(k≠j)2(k−j)e_j=0. Every 2(k−j) is nonzero in C because k≠j, and e_j≠0 by F001; hence a_j=0. This also covers λ=0, when the operator product is the identity. Discharge L1: a zero linear combination has all coefficients zero. Since a and j were arbitrary, the indexed family (e_i)_(0≤i≤λ) is complex linearly independent.

produces.statement: The family (e_i)_(0≤i≤λ) is complex linearly independent.

argument.text: Apply M001 with scalar field C, ambient space V, finite index type {0,…,λ}=Fin n, and vector family e restricted to that index set. H002 supplies dim_C V=λ+1 and finite dimension; H001 gives n=λ+1, so the number of indices is its dimension. F002 supplies independence. M001 yields span_C{e_i:0≤i≤λ}=V, hence these independent vectors form a basis.

produces.statement: The family (e_i)_(0≤i≤λ) is a complex basis of V.

argument.text: Set z=y^(λ+1)v and expand z=Σ_(i=0)^λ b_i e_i using F003. F001 gives hz=(−λ−2)z. Subtracting this from the h-action on the expansion and using independence gives 2(λ+1−i)b_i=0 for each i≤λ. This scalar is nonzero in C, so every b_i=0 and z=0. All further y powers on v vanish. From F001 and the definitions, xe_0=0 and xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ; directly from factorials ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, while z=0 gives ye_λ=0. Together with the h formula these are all asserted generator actions.

produces.statement: For 1≤s≤λ, xe_s=(λ−s+1)e_(s−1), and xe_0=0. For 0≤s<λ, ye_s=(s+1)e_(s+1), and ye_λ=0; he_s=(λ−2s)e_s for all 0≤s≤λ.

argument.text: For every 0≤i≤λ and r≥0, repeated use of F004 gives x^r e_i=[(λ−i+r)!/(λ−i)!]e_(i−r) if r≤i, and zero if r>i because x kills e_0. Similarly y^r e_i=[(i+r)!/i!]e_(i+r) when i+r≤λ, and zero past the top endpoint because y kills e_λ. These products follow by induction on r, starting with the empty product and multiplying the next coefficient at each step. Divide by r! in C, which is nonzero. Apply M005 first to its natural parameters (λ−i+r,r) when r≤i and second to (i+r,r) when i+r≤λ; the second parameter is at most the first in both cases. The identity choose(N,r)r!(N−r)!=N! identifies the respective scalar ratios as binom(λ−i+r,r) and binom(i+r,r). Thus the X_r,Y_r formulas hold with exactly the zero cases stated in the output statement. F003 and F004 supply its other clauses.
